EN_MODERN.text: “Oholah played the prostitute when she was mine. She doted on her lovers, on the Assyrians her neighbors,
EN_MODERN.commentary: This chapter is an allegorical passage where the prophet Ezekiel uses the metaphor of two sisters, Oholah and Oholibah, to represent the capitals of the northern and southern kingdoms of Israel (Samaria and Jerusalem) and their perceived political and religious alliances with foreign powers. In this verse, Oholah (representing Samaria) is accused of breaking her covenant with God by pursuing political and cultural alliances with neighboring Assyria.

EN_MODERN.text:
May He grant you your heart’s desire,
and fulfill all your counsel.
EN_MODERN.commentary: Psalm 20 is a communal liturgy in which the congregation offers prayers and sacrifices for the king before he goes into battle, asking God for victory and divine protection. In this context, the verse is part of a priestly or congregational blessing pronounced over the monarch, asking that God grant him success in his strategic plans and desires for the upcoming military campaign.

EN_MODERN.text:
He called the multitude to himself with his disciples, and said to them,
“Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
EN_MODERN.commentary: Mark 8 marks a turning point in the narrative where Jesus begins explicitly predicting his upcoming suffering and death to his disciples. Within this context, Jesus outlines the cost of discipleship to the gathered crowd, stating that loyalty to his mission requires personal sacrifice and hardship.

EN_OLD.text: And I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take the stony heart out of their flesh, and will give them an heart of flesh:
EN_OLD.commentary: Ezekiel 11 records the prophet's judgment against the corrupt leaders of Jerusalem alongside a promise of future restoration for the exiled Israelites. Within this context of predicted national renewal, the verse states that God will transform the people's rebellious disposition by replacing their hardened nature with a responsive and obedient spirit.

EN_OLD.text:
Who hath wrought and done
it, calling the generations from the beginning? I the LORD, the first, and with the last; I
am he.
EN_OLD.commentary: Chapter 41 of Isaiah records a courtroom-style challenge from God to the nations and their idols, urging them to consider who directs history and raises up conquerors like Cyrus the Great. Within this context, verse 4 asserts that Israel's God is the sovereign architect of human history and the eternal constant from the beginning to the end of time.

EN_OLD.text:
No man, when he hath lighted a candle, putteth
it in a secret place, neither under a bushel, but on a candlestick, that they which come in may see the light.
EN_OLD.commentary:
**Context of the Chapter:**
Luke 11 records various teachings and interactions of Jesus, including instructions on prayer, responses to critics who attribute his miracles to demonic power, and warnings against hypocrisy and seeking signs. In this section, Jesus uses common domestic metaphors to address how people receive and respond to his message.

**Context of the Verse:**
Within this passage, Jesus uses the example of a lit lamp to illustrate that his teachings and presence are meant to be openly displayed rather than hidden. He argues that just as a lamp is placed on a stand to illuminate a room, his message is intended to be clearly seen and understood by those around him.

NL_OLD.text: Gilead is mijne, Manasse is mijne, en Efraim is het hoofd mijnes hoofds; Juda is mijn wetgever.
NL_OLD.commentary: Psalm 108 is een lof- en smeeklied waarin de psalmist Gods hulp inroept en Zijn majesteit bezingt, met de overtuiging dat God zijn volk de overwinning zal schenken over zijn vijanden. In dit specifieke vers worden verschillende historische en geografische gebieden in Israël genoemd om Gods soevereiniteit en claim over het hele land te illustreren.

NL_MODERN.text:
Neem mijn ziel niet weg met zondaars,
en mijn levenslot niet met moordenaars.
NL_MODERN.commentary: Psalm 26 is een gebed waarin de dichter zijn onschuld en integriteit betuigt tegenover God, en waarin hij vraagt om vrijspraak en bescherming tegen de goddeloze mensen in zijn omgeving. In dit specifieke vers smeekt hij God om hem niet hetzelfde lot te laten ondergaan als zondaars en moordenaars, waarmee hij zich feitelijk distantieert van hun gedrag en straf.

NL_MODERN.text: Luister naar raad en neem aanneming van onderricht, zodat je in de toekomst wijs zult zijn.
NL_MODERN.commentary: Spreuken 19 is een verzameling van losse, praktische wijsheidsspreuken die het dagelijks leven, menselijke relaties en moreel gedrag betreffen. Dit specifieke vers benadrukt het belang van openstaan voor advies en onderwijs als noodzakelijke stap om op de lange termijn verstandige keuzes te maken.

Achis vroeg: ‘Wie heb je vandaag overvallen?’
David antwoordde: ‘Het zuidgebied
NL_MODERN.commentary: In 1 Samuel 27 zoekt David bescherming tegen koning Saul bij de Filistijnse koning Achis van Gat, en vestigt hij zich in de stad Ziklag. In dit vers ondervraagt Achis David over zijn militaire strooptochten, waarop David antwoordt dat hij plundert in het zuidelijk gebied van Juda, terwijl hij in werkelijkheid bondgenoten van de Filistijnen aanvalt.
